headline: Revenue returns to growth; acquired R&D hits earnings
summary_short: Revenue rose 11% to $2,804M, led by a 49% jump in Growth Portfolio revenue to $1.26B. Non-GAAP EPS fell 46% to $2.62 after $284M of acquired IPR&D, upfront and milestone expense.
summary_long: Spinraza grew 23% to $461M and Leqembi in-market sales grew 67% to $202M, while Vumerity fell 11% on U.S. formulary dynamics. The Apellis products Syfovre and Empaveli added $191M and $52M in their first full quarter. Multiple sclerosis revenue fell 13% to $919M. Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance's low end rises to $12.20-$13.00 from $12.00-$13.00.
confidence_notes: Non-GAAP EPS excludes transaction-related charges but includes $284M of acquired IPR&D, upfront and milestone expense. Apellis prior-period figures come from Apellis's Q3 2025 10-Q. Growth Portfolio includes Biogen's 50% share of Leqembi collaboration.

drivers.explanation: First full quarter of Apellis products plus growth in Spinraza, Skyclarys and Leqembi, partly offset by a 13% decline in multiple sclerosis revenue.
$284M of acquired IPR&D, upfront and milestone expense, primarily the RayThera acquisition, versus $2M a year earlier.
CEO says Biogen has returned to growth, with about 50% year-over-year growth in growth products and multiple Phase 3 readouts expected over the next 12 months.
